newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 6.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO DAILY -- After meetings between the Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa and Chinese officials, Beijing agreed to fund the future Special Administrative Region government and the provisional legislature before the handover.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- A long biographical political lyrical poem called Deng Xiaoping was recently published in China. Containing more than 6,000 lines, the poem was written by a young poet in Wuhan province who spent eight years on it.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Chief-executive designate Tung Chee-hwa said economic and cultural exchanges between Hong Kong and Taiwan would be strenthened after the handover, which would be good for the peaceful reunification of Taiwan.

-- MING PAO -- While the Hong Kong government was still considering what car to allocate to chief-executive designate Tung Chee-hwa, it has decided to buy new BMWs for government directors costing about HK$1 million.

-- Research show that despite dramatic lifestyle changes, only 10 percent women in major Chinese cities wear make-up and half of them have never tried any cosmetics. Those who wear make-up are mostly high income earners.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The salary increase of Cathay Pacific staff was three percent lower than last year. Staff with average performance were given about six per cent increase.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- A survey of the territory's leading stock broking and funds management firms showed that the Hong Kong share market was poinsed for a period of strong growth during the run-up to the handover.
-- Qinghai Aluminium Industry Corp, which would be the first overseas-listed company from China's backward west, planned to raise 500 million yuan in a Hong Kong listing.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Energy experts said that China would be forced to step up crude oil imports this year to keep pace with growing domestic demand.
